# Bench-pod SPI command protocol

The STM32H563 is the SPI master and the iCE40 the slave (`spi_slave.v`, decoded by
`cmd_dispatch.v`). One transaction is one command: CSn falls, the first byte is the opcode,
the payload follows, and reply bytes shift out on MISO while the master clocks dummy bytes.
CSn rising ends the command; an unknown opcode is ignored until then. Multi-byte fields are
little-endian. Bulk data does not go over this link: captures and deep-replay waveforms move
through the shared PSRAM, which the STM32 reads and writes over its own XSPI port.

"vNN" is the gateware version (the VERSION reply) a command or behavior first appeared in.
The firmware reads it at boot and gates newer commands on it (`*_MIN_GW` in
`stm32h563/src/signal_engine.h`). The three images (loop, deep and, from v54, emulation)
report the same version, so image-specific commands are gated on FPGA_FEATURES instead. v54
moved the emulated sensors (every I2C_*, EMU_*, SPIT_* and UART2_* command) into the emulation
image only; the loop and deep images ignore those opcodes.

| Opcode | Command | Payload (master to FPGA) | Reply (MISO) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x01 | PING | none | 0xA5 |
| 0x02 | VERSION | none | version byte (GATEWARE_VERSION in top_v2.v) |
| 0x03 | STATUS | none | flag byte: bit0 DAC running, bit1 capture busy, bit2 capture done, bit3 step train busy, bit4 SWD armed, bit5 sticky capture overflow (dropped bytes, an overlapping arm, or from v43 a writer burst cut because the STM32 took the bus; cleared by the next arm), bit6 control loop tripped (v30), bit7 always 0 (a 1 means the iCE40 is not driving MISO) |
| 0x10 | LOAD_WAVE | len(2) + N data bytes | none (fills the 4 KB waveform BRAM: up to 2048 16-bit samples for START_DAC, or the control loop's curve) |
| 0x11 | START_DAC | period(2) + divider(2) | none (shallow: loops the LOAD_WAVE BRAM, period in samples, <= 2048. A DAC sample takes max(divider, 3) + 51 clk48: v34+ floors the divider at 3 for the DAC8551's frame-gap timing (t9), earlier gateware at 0. v40+: the wire carries divider - 1 (the reload), and the gateware floors it at 2) |
| 0x12 | STOP_DAC | none | none (also leaves deep replay and the control loop, and cancels a start staged by DAC_ARM_ON_CAPTURE) |
| 0x13 | START_DAC_PSRAM | base(3) + count(3) + divider(2) | none (v17+; DEEP replay: the iCE40 streams the waveform straight out of PSRAM, up to the full 8 MB / 4,194,304 16-bit samples; the MCU stages it into PSRAM over XSPI first; divider as START_DAC. Deep image only (FPGA_FEATURES bit1)). v52+: sent over a running replay it restarts the stream at the new base and length; until v51 the reader kept its old position, so STOP_DAC had to come first |
| 0x14 | SET_DAC_STOP_AFTER | cycles(4) | none (v21+; arms the iCE40 to cut a concurrently running DAC `cycles` of the 24 MHz clk after the NEXT capture's t0, so the captured window shows the DAC switch off; cycles=0 disarms; send BEFORE the capture arm. v40+: one-shot, the capture's end clears it; until v39 it re-applied to every later capture) |
| 0x19 | DAC_ARM_ON_CAPTURE | none | none (v27+; CO-TRIGGER: defer the NEXT DAC start (START_DAC / START_DAC_PSRAM) so it fires on the SAME hardware cycle as the next capture's t0 instead of immediately: DAC sample 0 == capture t0, sample-exact and jitter-free. The deep reader still prefills its FIFO at the (suppressed) start, so the first PSRAM sample pops at t0 with zero latency. Consumed by that one arm; STOP_DAC cancels a staged but uncaptured start. Sequence: [stage waveform], DAC_ARM_ON_CAPTURE, START_DAC(_PSRAM), SET_DAC_STOP_AFTER, CAPTURE) |
| 0x16 | DAC_PROBE | none | v(2): the control loop's current DAC output (telemetry; pair with DAC_LOOP_IN_PROBE for the input it came from). Only meaningful on the loop image: the deep image has no loop engine and returns a tied-off 0, indistinguishable from 'the loop is holding 0 V'. Check FPGA_FEATURES bit0 first (the firmware refuses dac_loop_probe otherwise) |
| 0x1A | DAC_LOOP_SRC | src(1: 0=ADC, 1=fixed, 2=sweep) + fixed(2) + step(2) | none (v29+; selects WHERE THE CONTROL LOOP'S INPUT COMES FROM. 0 = the live ADC (closed loop, the pre-v29 behavior and the power-on default). 1 = the `fixed` register (OPEN loop: the host holds one point of the curve so the DAC output can be metered against curve[fixed] with the ADC and analog front end out of the picture; the first bring-up test of a curve or output path). 2 = an internal accumulator that adds `step` to the input every control tick, mod 65536 (OPEN loop function of TIME: walks the whole curve at a deterministic rate, again with no ADC). `fixed` is also the sweep's START value. Legal whether or not the loop is armed: a RUNNING loop picks the new source/value up on its next tick, so the host can step through curve points without re-arming or re-uploading the curve. Registers persist across arms) |
| 0x1B | DAC_LOOP_IN_PROBE | none | in(2): the input value the control loop's LAST TICK actually indexed the curve with, whatever the source. In a fixed/sweep run there is no ADC in the path at all, so this (not ADC_PROBE) is the loop's input. (v29+; same image gate as DAC_PROBE) |
| 0x18 | FPGA_FEATURES | none | features(1): which optional blocks THIS image carries: bit0 = closed-loop DAC (loop image), bit1 = deep DAC PSRAM replay (deep image), bit2 = sensor emulation (emulation image, v54). The images report the same VERSION, so gate on this, never on the version. The firmware swaps images by rewriting the iCE40 config flash and reconfiguring (JSON `fpga_image`), not with SB_WARMBOOT |
| 0x1C | DAC_LOOP_INMAP | in_zero(2) + in_gain(2, signed Q15) + in_trip(2) + flags(1: b0=map_en, b1=trip_en) | none (v30+; AFFINE MAP FROM THE RAW INPUT COUNT ONTO THE CURVE INDEX, plus an over-range trip. The loop indexes the curve with the raw input value, which on an inverting/offset/wrapping analog front end means a real measurement window lands backwards inside a few percent of the curve. This makes the index idx = sat_0_2047(((in - in_zero) * in_gain) >> 15), where the subtract is 16-bit MODULAR (for a window under 32768 counts that is exactly the unwrapped distance, so an ADC that wraps mid-range costs nothing) and in_gain is SIGNED so an inverting front end is just a negative gain. Saturation is the physical clamp: below the window = index 0 (source unloaded), above = 2047 (past short-circuit). abs(in_gain) <= 1.0 (32767) is all that is useful: one curve entry per input count is the hardware limit. flags b0=0 restores the legacy idx = in>>5 exactly. b1 arms the trip: at an index >= in_trip the loop LATCHES tripped, forces the output to vmin until disarmed, and raises STATUS bit 6, the guard for a loop driving a real pass device into a shorted DUT. Registers persist across arms; the map describes the BENCH, not the curve. Loop image only: the deep image does not decode it) |
| 0x15 | START_DAC_LOOP | k(2) + vmin(2) + vmax(2) + tick_div(2) | none (v23+; IN-FABRIC CONTROL LOOP: each tick it takes an INPUT (the live ADC by default; see DAC_LOOP_SRC 0x1A for the fixed/sweep open-loop sources, v29), indexes the LOAD_WAVE curve as a LUT (target = curve[index], index from DAC_LOOP_INMAP, in>>5 without a map), damps v += k*(target-v) [k Q15], clamps [vmin,vmax] and drives the DAC: a deterministic transfer function with no host in the control path (a solar-panel/MPPT emulator is one curve you can load). Load the curve with LOAD_WAVE first; stop with STOP_DAC. Uses NO PSRAM so an LA capture can run alongside. PRESENT ONLY IN THE LOOP IMAGE (FPGA_FEATURES bit0): the deep image ties the engine off and both images report the SAME version, so gate on FPGA_FEATURES, never on the version; arming on the wrong image otherwise looks like it worked and drives nothing. vmin must be <= vmax: the clamp tests vmin first, so an inverted window pins the output at vmin. k is used as k[14:0] (>32767 wraps to a small gain); tick_div < 8 outruns the pipelined tick) |
| 0x38 | DAC_CTRL | flags(1: bit0 = set the stream control byte, bit1 = send one frame now) + ctrl(1) + code(2) | none (v49+; the CONTROL BYTE of the 24-bit DAC frame, for the quad DAC8554 on the analog v3r2 board. bit0: every later DAC start (START_DAC, START_DAC_PSRAM, START_DAC_LOOP) streams {ctrl, sample} instead of {0x00, sample}; persistent, 0 at power-up, so a DAC8551 board that never sends this is unchanged. DAC8554: ctrl = 0x10 | channel << 1 (LD1:LD0 = 01, update that channel). bit1: one {ctrl, code} frame goes out at the next sample slot of a running stream (that sample and the rest of the stream play one slot later), or right away when the DAC is idle, so another channel can be set while one streams. A second frame sent before the first went out replaces it: with a stream running, wait one sample period between frames. ctrl 0x00 on a DAC8554 writes channel A's buffer without updating any output) |
| 0x20 | START_CAPTURE | count(2) + divider(2) | none. RETIRED in v40 (ignored): send CAPTURE 0x31 with la_cnt=0; the firmware sends 0x20 only to gateware <= v39. (16-bit shallow ADC. CAPTURE DIVIDERS (here, START_MEASURE cap_div, CAPTURE adc_div/la_div, LA_CAPTURE) are the sample PERIOD in 24 MHz clk: rate = 24 MHz / divider EXACTLY on v32+; ADC floors it at 60, LA at 2. Gateware <= v31 sampled every divider+1 clk, so the firmware sends divider-1 there. v40+: the LA divider is period - 2 on the wire, and the ADC one is not floored in gateware: the firmware floors it at 60) |
| 0x21 | ADC_PROBE | none | sample(2): live ADC, no PSRAM/CDC |
| 0x23 | CAPTURE_TEST | mode(1: 1=ramp self-test, 0=real ADC) | none (persistent: while 1, every capture records a known ramp (+0x0101 per sample) instead of the ADC, which tests capture, writer, PSRAM and XSPI read-back without the analog path) |
| 0x25 | PSRAM_CS | drive(1: 1=force PSRAM /CS low, 0=release) | none (boot self-test: does the iCE40 reach the /CE net?) |
| 0x30 | START_MEASURE | count(2) + dac_div(2) + cap_div(2) | none. RETIRED in v40 (ignored): DAC_ARM_ON_CAPTURE + START_DAC + CAPTURE (ADC only); the firmware sends 0x30 only to gateware <= v39. (DAC preloaded; 16-bit count; cap_div is a capture divider, see START_CAPTURE; dac_div is not: a DAC sample takes max(dac_div, 3) + 51 clk48, see START_DAC) |
| 0x31 | CAPTURE | adc_cnt(3) + adc_div(2) + la_cnt(3) + la_div(2) | none (unified ADC+LA arm: one t0 for both producers, two PSRAM regions; both counts 24-bit; divider = sample period, see START_CAPTURE. v40+: the only capture arm; a count of 0 leaves that producer off and keeps its divider. v50+: la_div = 0xFFFF selects the LA CHANGE capture: 48 MS/s, only the ticks where a channel changed are stored, 3 bytes each = {delta(10), state(14)} LE, la_cnt in units of 256 ticks (5.33 us); the first event has delta 0 (state at t0), a keep-alive event at least every 1022 ticks, an event on the last tick, then END = a later event with delta 0. The stream stops at the ADC base (SET_CAPTURE_BASES, latched at the arm): the firmware sets it to the end of the free LA space before a change capture. A full ring, or that end, stops the capture early with CAP_OVF; the stream up to END stays exact, and END's state field says why it ended: 0 the full duration, 1 the ring was full, 2 the region end). v52+: sample i of each stream is taken at t0 + (i+1) * its divider - 3 clk, so ADC and LA samples with the same divider share a clk edge; until v51 the ADC's sample 0 was the conversion in flight at t0 (up to one period early, or up to the previous capture's period late). v53+: a raw LA at divider 2 runs with the ADC; until v52 the ADC overflowed (CAP_OVF) as soon as both ran with the LA at divider 2 |
| 0x32 | SET_CAPTURE_BASES | la_base(3) + adc_base(3) | none (v22+; latches the PSRAM byte base of the ADC region for the next CAPTURE, so the firmware can place it below a resident deep-replay waveform; send BEFORE CAPTURE. la_base is ignored: the LA region always starts at 0) |
| 0x33 | SET_TRIGGER | channel(1: LA wire index 0..13 = LA1..LA14) + mode(1: 0=off, 1=rising, 2=falling, 3=high, 4=low) + flags(1: bit0 = pre-trigger, v50+; other bits reserved, send 0) | none (v35+; CAPTURE TRIGGER, gated start. Persistent until changed; applies to every later CAPTURE arm. With a mode set, the arm loads the producers but they start sampling only on the first clk cycle the condition holds on the synchronized LA levels; that cycle is t0, and the DAC co-trigger (DAC_ARM_ON_CAPTURE) fires and SET_DAC_STOP_AFTER counts from it. Re-arming with count 0 aborts a waiting capture. Mode 0 (and 5..7) = untriggered, identical to <= v34. Channels 14 and 15 read as 0. The firmware sends mode 0 after each triggered capture. Without flags bit0 there is no pre-trigger: the window is entirely POST-trigger, so the first sample is at t0. v50+: flags bit0 on an LA change capture (CAPTURE la_div = 0xFFFF) records from the arm and keeps the newest pre-trigger window in the LA ring (8192 words); only the post-trigger ticks count toward la_cnt, and the host finds the trigger la_cnt * 256 ticks before the stream's last tick) |
| 0x34 | TRIGGER_STATUS | none | status(1): bit0 = waiting for the trigger (armed, condition not seen yet), bit1 = a triggered capture fired since the last arm (v35+) |
| 0x40 | GPIO_SET | channel(0..13) + mode(0=low, 1=high, 2=hi-Z) | none |
| 0x41 | GPIO_STEP | channel + steps(2) + delay_us(2) | none (v40+: the wire carries the half-phase in us minus 1) |
| 0x42 | SET_LED | mask (bit0=green, bit1=yellow, bit2=red) | none |
| 0x43 | GPIO_GET | none | levels(2): live LA1..LA14 pin levels (bit n = LA n+1) through a 2-flop synchronizer, bits 15:14 = 0 (v35+) |
| 0x50 | SWD_ARM | swclk_ch + swdio_ch + nreset_ch(ignored since v37, send 0xFF) | none (nRESET is the pod's own pin, not an LA channel) |
| 0x51 | SWD_FEED | len(2) + N remote_bitbang bytes | none (in SPI mode: data bytes to shift out, <= 512 per feed) |
| 0x52 | SWD_READ | len(2) | N sample bytes (SWD), or the bytes clocked in (SPI mode), or 4 bytes per queued read (SWD_QFEED) |
| 0x53 | SWD_DISARM | none | none (releases the pins, SWD and SPI mode) |
| 0x55 | SPI_ARM | sck_ch + mosi_ch + miso_ch + cs_ch + half(24 MHz clk per half period, 2..63; v55+: 2..127, bit 7 ignored) + flags(bit0 = CPOL; v55+: bit1 = invert SCK for SPI modes 1 and 2, flags = CPOL | (CPOL xor CPHA) << 1; bit2 = I2C master) | none (v44+; CS starts released, driven high. v45+: bit 0 first on the wire, see the comment above. v55+ I2C master: sck_ch = SCL, mosi_ch = miso_ch = SDA, cs_ch = SCL again (read back for clock stretching), both open drain; SWD_FEED bytes are tokens 1 START, 2 STOP, 3 WRITE (the next byte is the data; reply {0, nack}), 4 READ+ACK, 5 READ+NACK (reply = the byte), MSB first on the wire, see i2c_master.v) |
| 0x56 | SPI_CS | level (1 = assert CS low, 0 = release high) | none (v44+; only change it while SPI_STATUS says idle) |
| 0x58 | SWD_QFEED | len(2) + transfers: request byte (the 8-bit SWD packet), + 4 data bytes for a write | none (v45+; needs SWD_ARM; the reply buffer gets 4 bytes per read, read back with SWD_READ) |
| 0x59 | SWD_QCONFIG | half(clk per SWCLK half period, 2..63) + idle(cycles after each transfer, 0..31) | none (v45+) |
| 0x5A | SWD_QSTATUS | none | qptr_lo(1) + flags(1): bit0 busy, bit1 stopped, bits4:2 the ACK of the last transfer, bit5 read parity error, bit6 qptr bit 8 (queue bytes consumed; a stopped transfer consumed its request byte only) (v45+); v55+: bit7 = the I2C master lost arbitration (its queue stopped; SPI_ARM clears it) |
| 0x57 | SPI_STATUS | none | status(1): bit0 = SPI mode armed (v55+: or the I2C master), bit1 = busy (bytes queued or shifting; v55+: or I2C tokens) (v44+) |
| 0x60 | I2C_CONFIG | target(0..3) + addr7 + sda_ch + scl_ch + flags + page + mask + drdy | none (v54+, emulation image only (FPGA_FEATURES bit2), like every I2C_*/EMU_*/SPIT_* command and UART2. Configures one of the 4 emulated I2C targets (sda_ch/scl_ch: LA wire index 0..13; targets may share a bus). flags: bit0 enable, bit1 16-bit register addressing (two pointer bytes, high byte first; the image is the 256-byte window whose high address byte is `page`, outside it reads 0x00 and writes are ignored), bits3:2 while_busy (0 flag: reads go on and BUSY registers OR in `mask`; 1 nack: a read address is not acknowledged while converting; 2 stretch: the read address is acknowledged, then SCL is held low until the conversion ends), bit4 mute fault (the address is not acknowledged), bit5 bus_stuck fault (SDA held low until a config clears it; the firmware bounds it). page: the high address byte of the 16-bit window; with 8-bit addressing (bit1 clear) its bits 1:0 select the pointer mode (v54, from firmware 3.10.2; earlier firmware sends 0): 0 bytes, 1 word registers (pointer p addresses image bytes 2p and 2p+1, MSB first, so 16-bit registers at consecutive pointers do not overlap and reads and writes run on into the next register; p bit7 is ignored, so 0x80..0xFF alias 0x00..0x7F), 2 command map (two pointer bytes h, l, high byte first: image byte h holds a base and the command points at image byte base XOR l, so 16-bit commands with any high bytes share the 256-byte image; the firmware lays out the bases and answers, and an unmapped h reads whatever its byte points at); 3 is the command map. drdy: bits1:0 data-ready mode (0 off, 1 pulse, 2 level), bit2 active high, bit3 assert at the end of each conversion; the pin is chosen with EMU_PINMAP. Rewriting the config of a running target keeps its bus state, so faults can be toggled mid-transfer. Until v53: one target, addr7 + sda_ch + scl_ch + flags + trig_reg + busy_reg + busy_mask + conv(2)) |
| 0x61 | I2C_DISABLE | target(0..3) | none (v54+: clears that target's enable bit only; until v53 no payload, the one target) |
| 0x62 | I2C_LOAD_REGS | target(0..4) + start_addr + len(2) + N data bytes | none (v54+: the register image of a target; target 4 is the SPI target. Each byte = the DATA byte of an image word; I2C_LOAD_ATTRS sets the attribute byte) |
| 0x63 | I2C_READ_REGS | target(0..4) + start_addr + len(2) | N bytes (v54+: read back the data bytes, DUT writes included) |
| 0x64 | I2C_STATUS | target(0..4) | pad(1) + flags(1) + wr_count(1) (v54+). The pad byte is sent while the target's snapshot loads. I2C targets: flags bit7 enabled, bit6 busy (converting), bit5 data ready asserted, bits4:2 bus state (0 idle, 1 address, 2 ack, 3 write, 4 stretching, 5 read, 6 read ack, 7 not addressed), bit1 the pointer is inside the image window. SPI target (4): flags bit7 enabled, bit6 CS asserted. wr_count counts the DUT's data bytes inside the window (mod 256; read-only registers included, pointer bytes not); it is also the write pointer of the target's write log (I2C_READ_LOG). Until v53: 7 bytes armed, xfer count(2), write count(2), last register, last value |
| 0x6A | I2C_LOAD_ATTRS | target(0..4) + start_addr + len(2) + N attribute bytes | none (v54+; the attribute byte of each image word: bit0 TRIG (a DUT write here starts a conversion), bit1 CMD (the DUT setting the pointer here starts one: commanded sensors), bit2 BUSY (while converting, reads OR in the target's mask), bit3 FIFO (reads pop the shared FIFO; the pointer does not advance past it), bit4 CLR (reading it clears a data-ready level), bit5 RO (DUT writes are not stored, still counted), bits7:6 TIME (which of the target's 4 conversion times TRIG/CMD start). The SPI target honours FIFO and RO only) |
| 0x6B | I2C_READ_ATTRS | target(0..4) + start_addr + len(2) | N attribute bytes (v54+) |
| 0x6C | I2C_TIMES | target(0..3) + index(0..3) + time_us(2) | none (v54+; conversion time `index` of a target, 0..65535 us; a TRIG/CMD register's TIME bits pick the index. A conversion reads as busy from the DUT's write until the time has passed) |
| 0x6D | I2C_DRDY | target(0..3) + action(1: 1 assert, 0 deassert) | none (v54+; firmware data-ready command: assert starts a pulse of EMU_CONFIG's width in pulse mode, or raises the level in level mode (a CLR register read or deassert drops it)) |
| 0x6E | EMU_PINMAP | 7 bytes: per LA wire 2c (low nibble) and 2c+1 (high nibble), a driver code | none (v54+; which emulated output owns each LA wire: 0 none, 1 I2C bus line (open drain: pulled low by any target configured on it, else released), 2..5 data ready of target 0..3, 6 the SPI target's MISO, 7 UART2 TX. Priority under SWD/SPI master and the stepper, over the UART proxy and GPIO_SET. Inputs (SCL, CS, SCK, MOSI, UART2 RX) need no entry. Power-up: all 0) |
| 0x6F | EMU_CONFIG | dr_width_us(1) + flags(1: bit0 flush the FIFO) | none (v54+; the data-ready pulse width of every target, 1..255 us, power-up 50; bit0 empties the shared FIFO) |
| 0x69 | LA_CAPTURE | count(3) + divider(2)  (24-bit samples; 2 B/sample) | none. RETIRED in v40 (ignored): send CAPTURE 0x31 with adc_cnt=0; the firmware sends 0x69 only to gateware <= v39. (Deep PSRAM stream up to 8 MB, the MCU reads it back over XSPI; divider = sample period, see START_CAPTURE) |
| 0x70 | UART_CONFIG | rx_ch + tx_ch + div(3) + flags | none (div = 24 MHz clk per bit, 2 .. 2^18-1; v40+ takes it as sent, the firmware clamps) |
| 0x71 | UART_DISABLE | none | none |
| 0x72 | UART_WRITE | len(2) + N data bytes | none (TX FIFO) |
| 0x73 | UART_READ | len(2) | N bytes (RX FIFO) |
| 0x74 | UART_STATUS | none | 3 bytes: rx_avail(2), flags: bit0 tx_full, bit1 tx_empty, bit2 rx_overflow (sticky; reading the status clears it), bit3 armed; v48+: bit4 UART2 tx_full, bit5 UART2 tx_empty, bit6 UART2 armed; v52+: bit7 rx framing error (sticky like rx_overflow: a frame's stop bit read low, a break or the wrong baud; that byte is dropped, and a held-low line is one error) |
| 0x75 | UART2_CONFIG | rx_ch + tx_ch + div(3) + flags | none (v48+; a second UART, for streams the pod sends the DUT while the UART proxy keeps its console, e.g. NMEA sentences of an emulated GPS receiver. Payload laid out as UART_CONFIG; flags bit0 = enable, so a config with enable 0 disarms it. v54+: emulation image only; RX on rx_ch (UART2_READ / UART2_STATUS), and TX reaches its pin through EMU_PINMAP code 7; until v53 TX only, rx_ch ignored and tx_ch driven directly) |
| 0x76 | UART2_WRITE | len(2) + N data bytes | none (v48+; UART2's 256-byte TX FIFO. UART_STATUS bit4 reports it full) |
| 0x77 | UART2_READ | len(2) | N bytes (v54+; UART2's 256-byte RX FIFO, like UART_READ) |
| 0x78 | UART2_STATUS | none | rx_avail_lo(1) + flags(1) (v54+): flags bit0 rx_avail bit 8, bit3 tx_full, bit4 tx_empty, bit5 armed, bit6 rx overflow, bit7 rx framing error (both sticky; reading the status clears them) |
| 0x7A | EMU_FIFO_WRITE | len(2) + N data bytes | none (v54+; push bytes into the shared 2048-byte sensor FIFO that FIFO registers pop; bytes beyond a full FIFO are dropped and set the overflow flag) |
| 0x7B | EMU_FIFO_STATUS | none | stat(2) (v54+), little-endian: bit0 the head byte is loaded, bits11:1 the bytes behind it (level = the two added, 0..2048), bit14 overflow (a push into a full FIFO), bit15 underflow (a FIFO register read while empty, which reads 0x00); both sticky, reading the status clears them |
| 0x79 | I2C_READ_LOG | target(0..4) + start(1) + len(2) | len bytes (v54+): the target's write log, a ring of 32 entries {address, value} (2 bytes each; address = the offset inside the window) at entry index wr_count mod 32: entry k holds the DUT's data byte number k (mod 32, counted like I2C_STATUS wr_count). start = 2 x the first entry index (mod 64, the ring wraps); like I2C_READ_REGS the first reply byte repeats, so ask for 2n + 1 bytes and drop the first. The firmware keeps its own count per target, reads the entries between it and wr_count, and has lost entries when wr_count moved by more than 32 since its last read (the rules of a sensor definition then see only the last 32 writes) |
| 0x7C | SPIT_CONFIG | cs_ch + sck_ch + mosi_ch + flags + read_bit + inc_bit + addr_mask | none (v54+; the emulated SPI target (register image, attributes, status and write log = target 4 of the I2C_* commands; only the FIFO and RO attributes apply). flags: bit0 enable, bit1 CPHA, bit2 CPOL (mode = CPOL*2 + CPHA), bit3 mute fault (MISO stays released), bits5:4 dummy bytes between the address and the data (0..3). The first byte of a transfer is the address byte: read_bit = bit position (bits2:0) + the value that means read (bit7); inc_bit = the same for an auto-increment flag, bit6 set when there is one (without one the address always increments); addr_mask = the address bits. CS active low; MISO goes out through EMU_PINMAP code 6, driven only while CS is low (0 during the address and dummy bytes and for writes). SCK up to about 2 MHz) |

## Retired opcodes

The gateware ignores these. Their values stay reserved.

| Opcode | Command | Removed in | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x17 | WARMBOOT | v24 | SB_WARMBOOT cannot work on this board: the iCE40 config flash shares the PSRAM bus. The loop and deep images are swapped by rewriting the config flash (JSON `fpga_image`). |
| 0x22 | READ_CAPTURE | v17 | captures are read back from PSRAM over XSPI, never through a BRAM read-back opcode. |
| 0x54 | SWD_STATUS | v17 | never sent by the STM32 firmware. |
